title: Inspect the working tree
summary: The working tree is the set of files you edit. status tells you what is new, changed or ready for a commit.
introduction: The working tree is the set of files you edit. status tells you what is new, changed or ready for a commit. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: The working tree is the set of files you edit. status tells you what is new, changed or ready for a commit.

blocks.code:
printf "My first note
" > note.txt
git status
blocks.title: Inspect the working tree

blocks.text: Git reports note.txt as untracked because it has not yet been added. The printf command is for a POSIX-style shell such as Git Bash.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Read note.txt and compare the status before and after creating another practice file.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Untracked files are not included in a commit unless you add them.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).

seo.title: Git: Inspect the working tree
seo.description: Learn about inspect the working tree in Git. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
